reviewMethod.methodNotesMd: Reviewed the Practitioner StructureDefinition findings, the two behavior findings whose `affectedResources` include `Practitioner`, and the shared Resource/DomainResource behavior findings only as context. The deterministic aggregate was treated as a prior, then compared after forming the resource-level judgment.

r4Maturity.effectMd: R4 Practitioner is a mature trial-use resource. That does not prohibit coherent R6 modeling changes, but it does mean hard wire-format changes, same-path semantic shifts, and avoidable operation/search breaks need concrete justification and transition support.

overall.oneLineConclusion: Practitioner keeps its identity and is mostly stable, with migration concentrated in communication reshaping/semantics and modifier-aware handling, so avoidable compatibility breaks still matter individually.

reasoning.thesisMd: Practitioner does not look like a resource-level redesign. R6 retains the same resource identity and most core demographic, identifier, address, telecom, name, qualification, and active data can move forward without a wholesale remap. The material local migration work is concentrated around `Practitioner.communication`, plus runtime handling for modifier semantics and downgrade handling for new R6-only safety/status fields.
reasoning.migrationShapeMd: The only hard R4-to-R6 instance break is `Practitioner.communication`: R4 represented each item as a `CodeableConcept`, while R6 represents each item as a backbone element with mandatory `language` and optional `preferred`. That is a real structure and SDK/codegen break, but it is targeted and often mechanically transformable. The binding strengthening on the nested language can make some migrated text-only or local-coded values invalid, and the semantic change means some patient-facing language data may belong on `PractitionerRole.communication`. `active` becoming a modifier and new optional `deceased[x]` affect safe processing and downgrade policy, but they do not force all R4 Practitioner instances through a broad content-model migration.
reasoning.compatibilityLeverageMd: Because the resource is not removed or broadly remodeled, a Practitioner migration program does not dominate the compatibility question. Systems using `communication` need a targeted migration, but that does not make additional low-cost preservation unimportant. FMM 3/trial-use creates meaningful pressure to preserve aliases, transition semantics, and query behavior when doing so does not defeat the R6 design.
reasoning.lessBreakingAlternativesMd: The full `communication` backbone redesign has a plausible R6 goal and only partial less-breaking alternatives because preserving the old `CodeableConcept` shape would create parallel representations for per-language preference. In contrast, the same-path semantic shift for `Practitioner.communication` remains standards-review-worthy because R6 could preserve the patient-communication meaning or introduce clearer separate administrative/correspondence-language guidance. The Measure `$collect-data` `practitioner` filter removal also has a low-cost compatibility option: keep `practitioner` as a deprecated alias for Practitioner reporter values.
reasoning.behaviorImpactMd: The direct behavior findings add localized API/search work rather than a resource migration program. The Measure `$collect-data` filter rename can break clients that pass `practitioner=Practitioner/{id}` and is avoidable enough to revisit. The SearchParameter expression-move finding is mostly a consequence of model changes; for Practitioner, `communication` search now indexes `Practitioner.communication.language`, so search indexes and compatibility servers must be updated alongside data migration. Shared Resource/DomainResource behavior findings, including generic `$meta`, `$validate`, and special search-parameter metadata changes, are relevant environment context but were not counted as Practitioner-specific drivers.
reasoning.comparisonToDeterministicAggregateMd: The independent review agrees with the deterministic aggregate's broad result: `majorMigrationAlreadyUnavoidable` should be `No`, the shape is `mostly-stable-with-local-breaks`, and compatibility should be assessed per change. The important nuance is that `communication` still needs real targeted migration and semantic review; the aggregate should not be read as saying there is no Practitioner migration work.
reasoning.uncertaintyMd: Confidence is high for the computable structure and behavior differences. Remaining uncertainty is mainly about official committee rationale, live terminology expansion behavior for `all-languages`, and real-world prevalence of R4 `Practitioner.communication` values and Measure `$collect-data` practitioner filtering.

findingConsiderations.title: Practitioner.communication changed from CodeableConcept to a BackboneElement with language and preferred children
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This is the main hard instance and generated-model break. It requires a targeted transform from `communication[]` as `CodeableConcept` to `communication[].language`, but the change is localized enough that it does not make a wholesale Practitioner migration unavoidable.

findingConsiderations.title: Practitioner communication language binding strengthened from preferred languages to required all-languages
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This can turn text-only or locally coded R4 communication values into R6 validation failures after the structural transform. It matters for migration cleanup, but it is path-local and its strictness has a plausible computability rationale.

findingConsiderations.title: Practitioner.communication semantic focus changed from patient communication to communicating with the practitioner
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This is the most standards-review-worthy Practitioner-specific issue. A same-path value can remain syntactically valid while changing business meaning, especially if R4 data represented patient-facing language capability that R6 now points toward `PractitionerRole.communication`.

findingConsiderations.title: Practitioner.active became a modifier element in R6
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: No R4 instance becomes invalid, but modifier-aware runtimes, summary views, and generated models must now treat `active=false` as non-ignorable. This is an implementation-safety update rather than evidence of broad model remodeling.

findingConsiderations.title: R6 adds Practitioner.deceased[x] as an optional modifier choice
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: The optional addition preserves forward R4-to-R6 validation, but because it is safety-relevant and a modifier, downgrade or mixed-version workflows need an extension or explicit loss policy. It does not drive the R4-to-R6 migration-program conclusion.

findingConsiderations.title: R6 adds Practitioner.qualification.status
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This optional non-modifier addition is mainly an R6-to-R4 round-trip concern for credentialing status. It is a local migration/downgrade chore, not a reason to treat Practitioner as broadly redesigned.

findingConsiderations.title: The `practitioner` filter is removed in favor of broader reporter/provider parameters
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This direct behavior finding is in scope because it affects Practitioner references in a Measure operation. It does not change Practitioner instances, but preserving `practitioner` as a deprecated alias for Practitioner reporter values looks low-cost and would reduce runtime/API breakage.

findingConsiderations.title: Many stable search codes now index different R6 element paths after resource model changes
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: For Practitioner, this includes search expression updates such as `communication` indexing `Practitioner.communication.language`. It should be handled with data/index migration and compatibility-server policy, but it mostly follows the targeted model changes rather than independently forcing a resource migration program.

findingConsiderations.title: Core special/profile search parameters changed type metadata for _content, _text, _query, and _profile
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This can affect generic Practitioner searches through shared infrastructure parameters, but it is a Resource/DomainResource-level behavior issue and should not be double-counted as a Practitioner-specific structural migration driver.

recommendedNextActions.actionMd: Review `Practitioner.communication` transition semantics: decide when R4 patient-facing language values should remain on Practitioner, move to `PractitionerRole.communication`, or be represented as administrative/correspondence language.
For Measure `$collect-data`, consider retaining `practitioner` as a deprecated optional alias for Practitioner reporter filtering to avoid a low-value runtime/API break.
Publish migration guidance and tests for wrapping `Practitioner.communication` values, validating BCP 47 language codings, and updating `communication` search indexes.

Define mixed-version and downgrade policy for `active` as a modifier, new `deceased[x]`, `communication.preferred`, and `qualification.status`, including extensions where loss would be unsafe or business-significant.

caveats: R6 input is ballot4, so final R6 content may still change.
No live terminology expansion was run for `all-languages`; terminology impact is based on package metadata and report evidence.
No production prevalence survey was available for R4 Practitioner communication values or Measure `$collect-data` practitioner filtering.
Shared Resource/DomainResource behavior findings were considered as context only and not scored as Practitioner-specific drivers.
